system.biography:
Monstrous scorpions are likely to attack any creature that approaches, and they usually charge when attacking prey.

Colossal 33 1d10 Con
Constrict (Ex)

A monstrous scorpion deals automatic claw damage on a successful grapple check.

Improved Grab (Ex)

To use this ability, a monstrous scorpion must hit with a claw attack. A monstrous scorpion can use either its Strength modifier or Dexterity modifier for grapple checks, whichever is better.

Poison (Ex)

A monstrous scorpion has a poisonous sting. The details vary by the scorpion’s size, as follows. The save DCs are Constitution-based. The indicated damage is initial and secondary damage.

Skills

A monstrous scorpion has a +4 racial bonus on Climb, Hide, and Spot checks.

system.description: You are skilled at using light weapons.
system.benefit: With a light weapon, rapier, whip, or spiked chain made for a creature of your size category, you may use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier on attack rolls. If you carry a shield, its armor check penalty applies to your attack rolls.
system.special: Natural weapons are considered light weapons.

system.description: Check: With each successful Climb check, you can advance up, down, or across a slope, wall, or other steep incline (or even a ceiling with handholds) at one-quarter your normal speed.
Make a Hide check to conceal yourself from enemies, slink past guards, slip away without being noticed, or sneak up on people without being seen or heard.
Your Spot check is either made against a DC that reflects how obvious the object is, or it is opposed by the target's Hide check.

What it does (SRD): If the creature hits with a listed natural weapon, it can attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking attacks of opportunity. Details (size modifiers, opposed checks, holding vs pinning) follow the grapple rules.

ThirdEra: This template has no numeric rows in Mechanical effects or Capability grants. Track grapple state in play; use the NPC’s natural attacks and CMB/CMD from the sheet when resolving the grapple.

What it does (SRD): On a successful grapple check, the creature deals extra bludgeoning damage (the amount is given in the creature’s stat block). Constrict usually requires a successful grapple after a grab-capable attack.

ThirdEra: Leave Mechanical effects and Capability grants empty here; enter the printed constriction damage and any special rules in the NPC’s Description or natural attack notes so it matches the SRD stat block.

Poison (Ex): Sting delivers poison; Fort DC and Con damage vary by size (Tiny DC 12 / 1 Con; Small DC 12 / 1d2 Con; Medium DC 13 / 1d3 Con; Large DC 14 / 1d4 Con; Huge DC 18 / 1d6 Con; larger sizes per SRD table). Save DCs are Constitution-based.

Constrict & improved grab: See linked creature-feature items for grapple rules; constrict applies automatic claw damage on a successful grapple check.

Skills: +4 racial on Climb, Hide, and Spot checks.
